# Why must AMP motion data and discriminator features still be audited after explicit reference tracking is removed?

> **Current answer:** AMP learns the supported short state transitions in motion data as a style reward. It removes explicit clip/phase selection but turns foot slip, bad contact, and coverage gaps in the dataset into reward boundaries. Data version, feature map, sample interval, discriminator, and policy must be audited as one unit.

## Key terms

- Adversarial Motion Prior (AMP, 对抗运动先验)
- Style Reward (风格奖励)

## Applicable robots

- Simulated characters in the paper; robot transfer requires new retargeting, feasibility, and safety validation

## Applicable simulators

- Isaac Gym/IsaacGymEnvs AMP and equivalent matched environments

## Controllers and methods

- Goal-conditioned policy with adversarial motion prior
- Discriminator-based style reward

## Applicable environments

- Simulated physics-based character tasks with unstructured motion clips

## Assumptions

- Demonstration and policy transitions use identical feature maps, timing, joint order, and normalization.
- The motion dataset has been audited for artifacts and required behavior coverage.

## Diagnosis and verification

- First verify the applicable robot, simulator, controller, environment, and assumptions, then follow the evidence locators below to inspect the original experiment or implementation.

## Result

- AMP learns the supported short state transitions in motion data as a style reward. It removes explicit clip/phase selection but turns foot slip, bad contact, and coverage gaps in the dataset into reward boundaries. Data version, feature map, sample interval, discriminator, and policy must be audited as one unit.

## Limitations

- Demonstration and policy transitions use identical feature maps, timing, joint order, and normalization.
- The motion dataset has been audited for artifacts and required behavior coverage.
